title: Spandasandoha — Collection on the Primordial Vibration
author: Ascribed to Kṣemarāja
text:
The Spandasandoha is a brief text — one song in our transmission — ascribed to Kṣemarāja, dealing with spanda: the primordial vibration or stirring that is the very life of consciousness and the technical heart of the Spanda school. It declares Śiva alone victorious, possessing the spanda, self-established and tasting his own inner face; what the school calls the first movement of the Real is here given as self-recognition in act.

Its juice: spanda is not motion among things but the throb by which the divine self knows itself — the microsecond of self-touch that precedes all world. The collection's juice is that everything observed, from breath to insight, is that one vibration catching itself; to know spanda is to have caught the Real mid-wink.
